classification.difficultyReason: Each part requires establishing parallel lines from angle evidence before applying a parallel-line angle property.

content.prompt: In each diagram below, give a reason why $AB\parallel CD$. Hence, find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$. Give all reasons.

spec.description: Two horizontal lines with transversals UX and VW; all eight point labels and four angle labels retained. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: A,U,V,B are collinear; C,X,W,D are collinear. Angle AUX and angle UXW are 75 degrees; angle UVW is 98 degrees; angle VWD is theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal. $\theta=98^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).
answer.worked:
$\angle AUX=\angle UXW=75^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal.

$\theta=98^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Triangle OCD with A on OC, B on OD and internal segment AB. Source angle sectors and labels retained in black.
spec.mathematics: Angle OAB and angle OCD are both 50 degrees; angle CDO is 35 degrees; angle OBA is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and beta are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because corresponding angles are equal. $\beta=35^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel CD$).
answer.worked:
$\angle OAB=\angle OCD=50^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because corresponding angles are equal.

$\beta=35^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABDC with right-angle squares at A and C, alpha at B and 65 degrees at D; no shading.
spec.mathematics: AB and CD each meet AC at 90 degrees. Angle ABD is alpha and angle CDB is 65 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and alpha are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because co-interior angles are supplementary. $\alpha=115^\circ$ (co-interior angles, $AB\parallel CD$).
answer.worked:
$\angle BAC+\angle ACD=90^\circ+90^\circ=180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because co-interior angles are supplementary.

Co-interior angles on transversal $BD$ are supplementary because $AB\parallel CD$.

$$\begin{align*}\alpha+65^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Opposing triangles ABV and DCV share the intersection of AD and BC. Source point and angle labels retained.
spec.mathematics: AB and CD are horizontal. Angle BAV and angle CDV are 40 degrees; angle ABV is 30 degrees; angle VCD is gamma.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and gamma are visible.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal. $\gamma=30^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).
answer.worked:
$\angle BAV=\angle CDV=40^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$ because alternate angles are equal.

$\gamma=30^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).
